title: AI Observability Platform Selection Guide
summary: Select telemetry standards and products from the decisions operators must make, while minimizing sensitive-content collection and vendor lock-in.
prerequisites: Service objectives, critical user journeys, and incident questions
A data classification and telemetry retention policy
An inventory of model, retrieval, tool, gateway, and application boundaries

sections.title: Start with decisions and evidence, not a dashboard
paragraphs: Observability is the practice of understanding internal system state through telemetry such as traces, metrics, and logs. A trace is a collection of timed spans representing one operation across system boundaries. For this lesson, one trace represents one fictional AI request across application, gateway, provider, retrieval, tool, and terminal postcondition spans.

Every span uses a stable trace_id, a unique span_id, and a parent_span_id. The application span is the root and carries the end-to-end request latency. Child span latencies measure individual operations and may overlap, so adding child latencies does not produce request latency. OpenTelemetry defines trace concepts and generative AI semantic attributes that can support provider-neutral correlation.

Begin with decisions: Can the release proceed? Can an investigator follow one request across every required boundary? What end-to-end latency did users experience? Did a postcondition evaluation judge the answer acceptable? Did an infrastructure operation fail? What did the request cost? Did telemetry expose protected content or cross a tenant boundary?

Treat prompts, completions, credentials, access tokens, and personal data in logs as sensitive. Redact or omit them by default. Aggregates such as token counts, span latency distributions, request latency distributions, status counts, and cost totals can be safer than content logs, but they still require access controls, retention limits, deletion tests, and tenant isolation.

The worked case and all named platforms are fictional teaching data. No vendor or model was executed. Product coverage, production scale, availability, regional behavior, and price are UNKNOWN until dated first-party documentation and a deployment-specific pilot establish them.
sections.callout: Transferable rule: keep correlation identifiers, request outcomes, redaction policy, and exportable telemetry under application control. Do not substitute a pooled span percentile for a user-visible request percentile.

code.label: Filled fictional observability selection record, followed by reusable blank record
code.code:
FILLED RECORD
Record status: FICTIONAL TEACHING RECORD; expected calculations are derived from supplied fixture data and are not actual vendor or model evidence.
Task: Select telemetry platform for the fictional Support Answer service.
Scope: application, gateway, model provider, retrieval, policy tool, postcondition evaluator, tenants, EU and US regions, and cross-provider investigation. One trace represents one fictional AI request. The application span is the root and represents end-to-end request latency.
Permissions: allowlisted producers write; tenant-scoped operators read aggregates; approved incident responders read redacted spans; privacy administrators export and delete. Raw prompts, completions, credentials, access tokens, email addresses, phone numbers, and account identifiers are excluded.
Signal contract: stable trace_id; unique span_id within the candidate export; parent_span_id; kind; finite nonnegative latency_ms and cost_usd; quality in [0,1]; status exactly ok or error; optional retry_of. Required kinds are application, gateway, provider, retrieval, tool, and postcondition. A retry uses a new span ID and points to an earlier failed span of the same trace and kind.
Decision questions: release readiness, user-visible quality, request latency, infrastructure health, cost, privacy incidents, tenant isolation, deletion, export, and cross-provider investigation.
Hard gates: privacy_redaction=true; export_otlp=true; tenant_isolation=true; valid parent correlation; one application root and one terminal postcondition per trace; complete required span kinds; valid retry relationships; truthful reported aggregates; valid finite numeric fields and statuses.
Data policy: no sensitive content in telemetry by default. Retain fictional redacted traces for 7 days and aggregates for 30 days. These are exercise requirements, not vendor guarantees. Export, deletion, regional behavior, retention expiry, and outage behavior require separate tests.
Metrics contract: request percentiles use application-span latencies only; pooled span percentiles use all span latencies and are labeled span_p50_ms, span_p95_ms, and span_p99_ms; child spans may overlap and must not be summed as request latency. Quality is the mean of one terminal postcondition quality per trace. Infrastructure health is one minus errors divided by gateway, provider, retrieval, and tool span count. Score = 0.50*quality + 0.30*infrastructure_health + 0.20*(1-total_cost_usd).
Verification: Run the supplied standard-library exercise by saving the supplied fixture as fixture.json and evaluator as evaluate.py, then run python3 evaluate.py fixture.json. This is an offline simulator and requires no provider account, network, package, real credential, or model execution. Expected baseline output, not actual execution: Northstar TraceHub hard_gate=PASS request_p50_ms=500.000 request_p95_ms=590.000 request_p99_ms=598.000 span_p50_ms=50.000 span_p95_ms=480.000 span_p99_ms=576.000 quality=0.950 infra=0.778 cost_usd=0.550 score=0.798; OpenRelay hard_gate=PASS request_p50_ms=500.000 request_p95_ms=545.000 request_p99_ms=549.000 span_p50_ms=50.000 span_p95_ms=495.000 span_p99_ms=539.000 quality=0.750 infra=1.000 cost_usd=0.400 score=0.795; selected=Northstar TraceHub. The evaluator also expects REJECT for negative_latency, bool_latency, nonfinite_latency, negative_cost, unbounded_quality, invalid_status, missing_provider_span, duplicate_span_id, broken_parent, unknown_retry_target, malformed_record, misleading_aggregate, privacy_gate, export_gate, and tenant_gate. No actual execution is claimed here.
Worked decision trace: the supplied Northstar records have application latencies 400 and 600, giving request p50=500, p95=590, and p99=598 under rank (n-1)*q with linear interpolation. The evaluator's pooled span values are span p50=50, p95=480, and p99=576. Northstar quality=0.950, infrastructure health=0.778, cost=0.550, score=0.798. OpenRelay score=0.795. Both pass the fictional hard gates, so Northstar is selected by the illustrative formula only.
Malformed and misleading-input verification: reject negative, Boolean, or nonfinite latency; negative cost; quality outside [0,1]; invalid status; missing required span; duplicate span ID; broken parent; unknown retry target; malformed record; aggregate disagreement; privacy=false; export=false; and tenant_isolation=false. These are simulator checks, not provider guarantees.
Production evidence: UNKNOWN until dated access, redaction, OTLP export, tenant-isolation, retention-expiry, deletion, outage, alert, volume, cost, owner, and exit-plan tests are recorded for the selected deployment. A real result must include provider or deployment, date, tenant, request and trace identifiers, response, credential fingerprint where applicable, redacted export inspection, and billing or audit evidence.
Stop conditions: protected content appears; tenant separation fails; a required parent or retry link is missing; an aggregate conflicts with raw records; export, deletion, or retention test fails; telemetry becomes an unintended inference dependency; or a provider capability is assumed without dated evidence.
Recovery: disable the affected signal, restrict access, preserve an approved minimal incident record, delete exposed data under policy, rotate credentials if needed, and restore collection only after regression tests pass. Unless explicitly engineered and approved as a dependency, telemetry outage must not block the inference request path.
Sources: OpenTelemetry observability https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/observability/; traces https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/signals/traces/; OTLP https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otlp/; generative AI semantic conventions https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/blob/main/docs/registry/attributes/gen-ai.md; Python quantile reference https://docs.python.org/3/library/statistics.html#statistics.quantiles. OpenTelemetry sources describe concepts and protocol, not the fictional platform capabilities.

sections.title: Evaluate coverage, governance, and failure behavior
paragraphs: The fixture below is fictional and deliberately small. Each trace contains application, gateway, provider, retrieval, tool, and postcondition kinds. Trace n1 also contains a provider retry. The retry has a new span_id and retry_of points to the earlier failed provider span. A retry must never reuse the original span_id because duplicate identifiers make correlation ambiguous.

The evaluator treats application-span latency as end-to-end request latency. It separately computes a distribution over all span latencies and labels those fields span_p50_ms, span_p95_ms, and span_p99_ms. A pooled span percentile is never described as user or request latency.

User-visible quality is the arithmetic mean of one terminal postcondition quality value per trace. Infrastructure-span quality fields are fixed at 0.0 and are not averaged. Infrastructure health is one minus the error fraction across gateway, provider, retrieval, and tool spans. Application and postcondition statuses are excluded from that infrastructure denominator.

Percentiles use sorted linear interpolation with rank (n - 1) times q. For example, application latencies 400 and 600 have p50 500, p95 590, and p99 598. This stated convention is part of the exercise contract and is not a claim about every product's percentile implementation.

The candidate records include reported aggregates so the evaluator can compare rendered claims with raw evidence. A disagreement is a hard rejection. The fixture also declares privacy redaction, OTLP export, tenant isolation, retention, and deletion requirements. These declarations are exercise inputs, not proof that a real product provides the capability.
sections.callout: Logs containing prompts or credentials are sensitive content. Aggregate latency, status, quality, and cost metrics are different signals, but they are not automatically anonymous or safe.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Save the previous code object as fixture.json and the following code object as evaluate.py in the same directory. Run `python3 evaluate.py fixture.json`. Only Python 3 standard-library modules are used.

The program validates exact record fields, finite nonnegative latency and cost, bounded quality, the exact ok or error status enum, unique span IDs, parent correlation within each trace, one application root and one postcondition per trace, every required span kind, and retry targets that are earlier failed spans of the same kind and trace. It rejects privacy, export, tenant, correlation, and aggregate failures before score comparison.

The verifier contains assertions for the percentile convention, every supplied negative case, and the complete expected stdout. If a supplied negative case is accepted or the exact baseline output changes, the process raises AssertionError and exits unsuccessfully. The `--explore` option retains negative-case assertions but disables only the baseline stdout comparison so learners can inspect changed inputs.

Expected stdout for the unmodified fictional fixture is shown below. This is a derived expectation established by inspecting the fixture and formulas. It is not a claim that the code was actually executed:
`candidate=Northstar TraceHub hard_gate=PASS request_p50_ms=500.000 request_p95_ms=590.000 request_p99_ms=598.000 span_p50_ms=50.000 span_p95_ms=480.000 span_p99_ms=576.000 quality=0.950 infra=0.778 cost_usd=0.550 score=0.798`
`candidate=OpenRelay hard_gate=PASS request_p50_ms=500.000 request_p95_ms=545.000 request_p99_ms=549.000 span_p50_ms=50.000 span_p95_ms=495.000 span_p99_ms=539.000 quality=0.750 infra=1.000 cost_usd=0.400 score=0.795`
`selected=Northstar TraceHub`

`negative=bool_latency result=REJECT`
`negative=nonfinite_latency result=REJECT`
`negative=negative_cost result=REJECT`

For production evidence, add dated access tests, redaction tests, OTLP export inspection, retention-expiry tests, deletion verification, outage behavior, alert precision, volume, cost, owner, and exit plan. Stop affected collection if protected content appears, tenant separation fails, or required deletion cannot be enforced.
sections.callout: Failing closed for platform selection does not require failing inference closed. Unless telemetry is an explicitly engineered service dependency, an observability outage should not block the user's request path.

sections.title: Independent changed-input task
paragraphs: Make a copy of fixture.json. Change only the four Northstar fields listed below. Do not change OpenRelay, the retry relationship, any postcondition quality, or any negative case.

Run `python3 evaluate.py changed-fixture.json --explore`. Record the displayed hard-gate result, selected candidate, and all negative-case results. Independently recompute Northstar's request p50, p95, and p99, pooled span p50, p95, and p99, postcondition quality, infrastructure health, cost, and score from the changed raw records.

Explain every reason Northstar is ineligible in the first run. Explain why changing a raw application latency requires recomputing request and pooled span aggregates, while changing an infrastructure status affects infrastructure health. Explain why neither better latency nor a higher score overrides a privacy hard gate.

For a second run, restore privacy_redaction to true and replace the misleading reported_request_p50_ms with the value computed from the changed application-span records. Run with `--explore` again. State the selected candidate and support the decision with the recomputed measures.
sections.callout: A changed raw record is evidence. A manually changed aggregate is only a claim until it matches recomputation from those records.

code.label: changed-input-task.txt
code.code:
First changed-input run, Northstar only:
1. n1-tool.status: "error" -> "ok"
2. n2-app.latency_ms: 600 -> 500
3. reported_request_p50_ms: 500 -> 999
4. privacy_redaction: true -> false

Run:
python3 evaluate.py changed-fixture.json --explore

Second-run repair:
1. privacy_redaction: false -> true
2. reported_request_p50_ms: replace 999 with the p50 recomputed from the changed application spans

Do not change reported_span_p50_ms unless your recomputation proves it changed. Do not change OpenRelay or any negative case.

sections.title: Answer key and actionable feedback
paragraphs: In the first changed-input run, Northstar is rejected because privacy_redaction is false and reported_request_p50_ms is 999 while the changed application latencies are 400 and 500. Their request p50 is 450, not 999. OpenRelay remains eligible and is selected. Every supplied negative case must still report REJECT.

For changed Northstar, request p50 is 450, request p95 is 495, and request p99 is 499. Across all thirteen span latencies, pooled span p50 remains 50, pooled span p95 becomes 440, and pooled span p99 becomes 488. These pooled span values are not user-request percentiles.

Postcondition quality remains 0.950 because neither terminal postcondition changed. Infrastructure health becomes 0.889 when the n1 tool status changes from error to ok: one error remains among nine gateway, provider, retrieval, and tool spans. Total cost remains 0.550. The illustrative score becomes 0.832 after rounding: 0.50 times 0.950 plus 0.30 times eight ninths plus 0.20 times 0.450.

The application-latency improvement changes latency measures but does not directly change this exercise's score because the stated formula has no latency term. The status repair raises the score through infrastructure health. Neither effect makes a candidate eligible while privacy redaction is false or a reported aggregate contradicts raw records.

For the second run, set privacy_redaction to true and reported_request_p50_ms to 450. Northstar then passes with request p50 450, request p95 495, request p99 499, span p50 50, span p95 440, span p99 488, quality 0.950, infrastructure health 0.889, cost 0.550, and score 0.832. Northstar is selected over unchanged OpenRelay at 0.795.

If your values differ, first sort the relevant values, apply rank (n - 1) times q, and interpolate. Use only application spans for request latency, only postconditions for quality, and only gateway, provider, retrieval, and tool statuses for infrastructure health. Check hard gates before comparing scores.

sections.title: Transfer the method across providers without inventing coverage
paragraphs: Keep application-generated trace_id, span_id, parent_span_id, schema version, provider identifier, model identifier, operation name, status, duration, retry relationship, and postcondition fields under your control. OpenTelemetry's generative AI semantic conventions provide a vocabulary for generative AI telemetry, while OTLP specifies an export protocol.

The same contract can be tested when moving among OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, local Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral, Phi, NVIDIA, or Z.ai deployments. This transfer statement does not claim that those providers expose equivalent tracing, OTLP export, redaction, evaluation hooks, or correlation support.

Equivalent support for the named providers and deployments is UNKNOWN in this lesson except where a cited first-party source describes a particular product. Establish each capability with dated first-party documentation, source code where applicable, and the same end-to-end redaction, parent-link, retry, tenant, export, deletion, retention, and outage tests.

OpenAI's cited Agents SDK documentation and Cloudflare's cited AI Gateway documentation describe their respective products only. They do not prove feature parity for Anthropic, Google, Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral, Phi, NVIDIA, Z.ai, or any custom deployment.

Telemetry should not become an accidental required path for inference. Test destination outages and define whether approved telemetry is queued, sampled, or dropped. Preserve the request path unless blocking behavior is an explicit, reviewed service requirement.
sections.callout: UNKNOWN is an actionable result. Record the missing evidence and test needed instead of assuming compatibility from a model or provider name.

sources.title: Python statistics: quantiles and inclusive interpolation
